## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Piṇḍukkhepaka-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 44) is an etiquette training rule (*sekhiya*) preserved in the Theravāda *Vinaya Piṭaka*. Titled "Eating from lifted mouthfuls" in modern translation, the rule regulates proper conduct and decorum for Buddhist monastics while partaking of almsfood, specifically addressing the habit of lifting or tossing mouthfuls of food into the mouth. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within the Pali canon, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Sekhiya 44, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha Sekhiya 44, and the respective Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra summaries. Beyond the Theravāda lineage, parallel regulations survive in Sanskrit and Chinese across several early Buddhist monastic codes: the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya (e.g., Lzh Dg Bu Vb Sk 39), the Mahīśāsaka Vinaya (e.g., Lzh Mi Bu Vb Sk 75), and the Mahāsāṅghika and Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda Vinayas (e.g., Lzh Mg Bu Vb Sk 31, San Mg Bu Pm Sk 32, San Lo Bi Vb Sk 33).
